detailed_descriptions.en: Explore the vast outdoors of North America in this next level open world hunting game. Feel the thrill of the hunt and keep an eye out for the wild and wonderous species that are roaming the wilderness. Hunt in North America and display big game like Moose, Elk, Bears, and Bison as well as, smaller animals like Rabbits, Turkeys and various other birds. Venture to Africa and hunt some of the most dangerous and diverse species yet, including massive hippos, thunderous buffalo, prowling lions, and deadly Nile crocodiles. As the ultimate hunting simulator, Way of the Hunter 2's goal is to become the most authentic and advanced virtual hunting experience. Building upon our previous experience, invaluable player feedback, and countless iterations this game will start as the foundation for many updates, expansions, and a true long-term support. As the new hunter in town, you are recruited to take on a series of unique challenges that span two breathtaking environments and introduce you to a cast of memorable NPCs. In New Laurentia, you’ll team up with a skilled dog trainer and assist the former warden as you uncover the mystery behind the unusual behavior of the local moose population. In Kilimaya Reserve, you will work for Hearth & Hunt in support of a renowned safari guide, meet an eccentric archery trainer and attempt to recruit a legendary retired huntress. Features: Hunting Dog: A loyal companion that detects animal signs, follows blood trails, and tracks wounded game. With regular exercise and training, it grows more skilled over time. Shot review: Our improved bullet camera lets you break down every shot with precision. Analyze trajectory, speed, angle, placement, and more — learn how to make the perfect shot, every time. Hunting Lodge: Your hub for adventure. Plan hunts, display trophies, and unlock upgrades to build your hunting paradise. Each map has its own Lodge unique to that territory. High-Tech Equipment: Advanced gear sharpens your instincts, delivering a more immersive hunting experience with thermal night vision and enhanced reserve monitoring to manage habitats.
